clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today in the fermentation tanks regarding ethanol, and what decision would real-time ethanol data drive?
clarification_questions.why: Identifies the stakeholder pain and whether in-line monitoring is needed for process control or only for trend tracking, which determines the sensor choice.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Pain and decision unknown; a feasibility check with the expert will establish whether real-time data is needed before any purchase.

clarification_questions.question: What ethanol concentration range do you need to measure, and what is the lowest level that matters for your decision?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether the task is a percent-level or trace-level measurement, which decides whether Raman is suitable and what detection limit is relevant.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Level unknown; lab screening on representative wine samples establishes whether the required level is ppm or % level.

clarification_questions.question: Is the wine during fermentation clear, turbid or opaque, and does it contain gas bubbles or solids such as yeast and skins?
clarification_questions.why: Optical properties and suspended matter affect the signal, the probe geometry and the matrix calibration.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Optical state unknown; lab screening with turbid and bubbly samples is needed before selecting a probe geometry.

clarification_questions.question: What are the fermentation temperature range, the cleaning or sterilization procedure of the tank, and how much does the wine composition vary between batches?
clarification_questions.why: Temperature, cleaning chemicals and batch-to-batch matrix variation can change the signal and invalidate a calibration, and determine probe materials.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Conditions unknown; the calibration would need to be validated over several batches and cleaning cycles.

clarification_questions.question: Where would the probe be installed in the tank, and how far is the planned analyzer from the measuring point?
clarification_questions.why: Installation point and distance determine the probe type and whether a fiber link is needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation point and distance unknown; a probe and analyzer layout will be defined after the expert discusses the tank geometry.

clarification_questions.question: What reference method do you use today for ethanol, and what is its accuracy?
clarification_questions.why: A reference method is needed to compare the in-line results and to judge whether the sensor meets your need.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method unknown; the comparison design will be set up against the lab method the client uses.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget do you require for the in-line measurement?
clarification_questions.why: These requirements define whether a Raman system is an adequate solution and what can be specified in a purchase order.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; no detection limit, accuracy or part number can be stated until the requirements and a lab trial are defined.

flags_before_revision.detail: different_context: S01 p.16 supports Raman for glucose, acetate and lactate in bioprocess media. It does not mention ethanol, and it does not cover wine. The claim transfers the bioprocess example to ethanol in wine without saying so. Fix: State that the source supports Raman for bioprocess metabolites such as glucose, acetate and lactate. Say that its suitability for ethanol in wine is untested and must be checked on wine samples.

not_supported: S02 p.18 lists ethanol among analytes for some NIR-range bands. It does not say that NIR is lower-cost. The only cost advantage on that slide is for spectral IoT sensors versus a centralized analyzer. Fix: Remove the lower-cost claim. Keep only the statement that S02 p.18 associates ethanol with NIR bands, and mark cost as an open question to check.

not_supported: The cited pages give no Raman range in the fiber-transmission sense. DOCX §5 says Raman shift (cm-1) and laser excitation (nm) are stated separately, and S02 p.6 gives only fiber transmission windows. The claim that Vis-NIR silica covers the Raman range is therefore unsupported. Fix: Remove the Raman coverage statement. State the Raman shift and laser excitation separately, and check fiber coverage for the actual excitation and Raman shift range of the chosen configuration.

not_supported: S01 p.7 mentions sample inhomogeneity and process turbulence as factors to consider. It does not mention CO2 bubbles, and it does not say that yeast turbidity or turbulence can mimic composition changes. Fix: Limit the claim to what S01 p.7 supports: process turbulence and morphological factors complicate analysis. Present CO2 bubbles and yeast turbidity as hypotheses to test.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]
raman_fluorescence_background: Raman can be swamped by fluorescence background from many organic compounds; check signal quality first. [S01 p.11]

geometry_follows_optics: Clear liquids suit transmission or transflection; opaque, concentrated or powder samples suit diffuse reflection; highly absorbing or 'black' liquids suit ATR. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); S01 p.16; S01 p.17-18]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
